header: Date: 2026-03-15 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Emily Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Hydra), Priya Rao (Head InfoSec, Hydra), Daniel Wu (DevOps), Asha Menon (Product)
summary: Introductory security posture discussion. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for inference. Primary concerns: SOC 2 / ISO compliance, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption at rest/in transit with KMS integration, and data residency. Agreed next step: share SOC 2 artifacts, high-level private deployment diagram, and schedule technical deep-dive for benchmarking/POC scope.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Samir from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Liam: Liam here, CTO at Hydra.
[00:09] Priya: Priya Rao, head of InfoSec.
[00:11] Daniel: Daniel Wu, DevOps.
[00:13] Asha: Asha on product.
[00:15] Emily: Emily Chen, Systems Eng at Redwood.
[00:18] Samir: Awesome. Agenda — quick intro, review compliance posture questions (SOC2/ISO), SSO and RBAC, KMS/encryption, audit logs and retention, then next steps. Any additions?
[00:28] Priya: That's fine. We're mostly trying to validate that any vendor we pick can meet our governance needs, and to decide whether Hosted is viable or we need Private.
[00:36] Samir: Understood. Quick background on Redwood — we run Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments — same API surface. For security we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 in progress, SAML SSO via Okta, KMS integrations, and customizable retention. Emily, want to add on the infra side?
[00:55] Emily: Yeah, on the runtime side we have encryption in transit TLS 1.2+ and at-rest encryption on volumes. For Hosted customers we manage the keys but can offer customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM for Dedicated and Private. Also audit logs are streamed to customer S3 or to our log retention tier depending on contract.
[01:12] Priya: Quick question — your SOC2 report, is it available for customers?
[01:16] Samir: Yes, we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA or via our security portal. I'll send a summary today and attach the redacted report.
[01:24] Priya: Great. And ISO?
[01:26] Samir: We're in the final stages for ISO 27001, expecting certification Q2 2026. We'll share the statement of applicability when it's done.
[01:33] Daniel: For Private — what's the typical network model? VPC peering or private connector?
[01:38] Emily: Two common patterns: 1) Private deployment into your VPC — we ship a customer-managed control plane and inference workers run in your subnets (optionally on-prem via air-gapped package). 2) VPC peering or PrivateLink if you want managed but private connectivity. For Dedicated we also support VPC endpoints. There's a diagram I'll share.
[01:58] Liam: If we go Hosted, we need guaranteed region residency. We can't have EU data leave the region for certain PII workflows.
[02:05] Samir: We have region pinning for model routing and can route requests to specific geographic pools. For legal egress we can also do model variants in-region; we'll follow your residency matrix.
[02:15] Priya: Regarding keys — can you integrate with our AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault? We prefer customer-managed keys.
[02:22] Emily: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support AWS KMS and CloudHSM, and a bring-your-own-vault pattern for HashiCorp. Hosted can support BYOK for encryption-at-rest via KMS grants, but the handshake's slightly different — we'll detail in the doc.
[02:36] Priya: Do you support HSM-backed key wraps for models or tokenation?
[02:40] Emily: Yes, HSM wraps are supported in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have a KMS-backed envelope encryption but can establish HSM-backed consumer keys under a contract.
[02:49] Daniel: Audit logs — what granularity? We need per-request tokens, who called what model, latency, errors, and KV cache events if possible. Also retention config per dataset.
[02:58] Emily: Our audit logs include request metadata (timestamp, client id, route/model used, response code), token counts, and trace IDs. We can add structured events for cache hits/misses. For PII redaction we can filter fields before export. Retention is configurable per contract — default 90 days on Hosted, custom for Dedicated/Private.
[03:18] Priya: Is there an immutable audit trail and export to our SIEM?
[03:22] Samir: Yes, we support pushing logs to customer S3, Kafka, or SIEMs via connectors. For immutability we can integrate with WORM storage options on the customer's side.
[03:31] Liam: Is there RBAC at both team and token level? We want role separation between Junior SREs and Prod SREs.
[03:38] Emily: We provide RBAC in the Console with roles (Admin, Ops, Viewer, Billing). Tokens can be scoped to routes/models/quotas. For enterprise we support service roles and fine-grained IAM mappings via SCIM and SSO groups.
[03:52] Priya: SSO — SAML only? OIDC?
[03:55] Samir: SAML/SAML2 with Okta is most common. OIDC supported as well. SCIM for group sync, SAML assertions for role mapping. We also have MFA requirements configurable via the IdP.
[04:06] Priya: Any SOC2 controls covering third-party risk for your GPU providers? We need an inventory.
[04:12] Samir: We keep a third-party inventory and include vendor assessments in our SOC2. For Dedicated we can isolate vendors per deployment if required. We'll send a redacted vendor inventory for the scope.
[04:23] Asha: On data retention, product side — can we selectively retain embeddings or only short-term tokens? We want to avoid storing PII embeddings for more than X days.
[04:32] Emily: Yes, we have configurable retention per object type — raw requests, embeddings, model outputs. You can set a TTL; we also have the option to disable persistent logging for certain routes.
[04:43] Daniel: What's the path if we detect leakage or compromise — incident response?
[04:46] Samir: We have an incident response playbook, notify within 1 hour for Sev1, provide forensic artifacts, and coordinate with customer IR. Enterprise contracts include a runbook and joint tabletop exercises.
[04:57] Priya: Do you provide pen-test results or bug-bounty summary?
[05:00] Emily: We can share high-level summaries and remediation status. For specific reports we typically do this under NDA.
[05:06] Liam: On the performance side — if we run Dedicated or Private, can we run local model variants (quantized) that you support in your runtime? We need to benchmark latencies for 2k token sequences.
[05:16] Emily: Yes, our runtime supports quantized families, batching strategies, KV cache optimization. For POC we usually run a 2–4 week benchmark against representative prompts. We'll coordinate test harness and metrics.
[05:28] Daniel: About billing and audit trail — we want token-level cost visibility mapped to service tokens so we can show chargebacks.
[05:35] Samir: Console has token-level breakdowns by API key and route. For enterprise we can provide per-token cost attribution and exportable CSVs or BigQuery exports.
[05:45] Priya: For Hosted, what is your data isolation guarantee? Are tensors stored on shared volumes?
[05:50] Emily: For Hosted, inference nodes are multi-tenant but we isolate model sessions and ephemeral tensors are never persisted to shared durable storage. Persistent artifacts (logs, cache) are segregated per-tenant. If you need physical separation, Dedicated or Private gives dedicated pools.
[06:07] Liam: Our timeline — target proof-of-concept in April, production decision by June. Any blockers you foresee?
[06:14] Samir: Sounds reasonable. Blockers would be regulatory signoff on Hosted if the SOC2/ISO info doesn't meet your thresholds, or if your legal requires on-prem. We can usually mitigate with Dedicated or Private.
[06:25] Priya: A few nitty-gritty items from my list: 1) data residency: we need EU and US separation for certain workloads, 2) retention SLA and secure deletion certification, and 3) KMS key rotation policy and access logs.
[06:35] Emily: For residency we do region pinning and can set up Dedicated pools in EU and US. For deletion we provide APIs to purge data and attestations for deletion within defined windows. KMS rotation follows your KMS policy — we honor key rotation and maintain access logs via CloudTrail/Stackdriver exports.
[06:50] Priya: Secure deletion — can you provide a proof-of-deletion mechanism? Some vendors produce a signed assertion.
[06:55] Samir: We can provide deletion receipts and an audit trail showing deletion events. For highly-regulated customers we can add attestation clauses in the contract.
[07:04] Asha: Are there any data categories you treat differently, like health data or financial PII?
[07:09] Emily: We categorize sensitive data and have stricter handling for PHI/PCI-like data. For PHI we usually recommend Private deployment with customer-managed keys and stricter audit retention.
[07:20] Daniel: Do you support hardware attestation on the inference hosts?
[07:23] Emily: For Private we can run on your hardware or support TPM-based attestation in supported cloud providers; for Dedicated we can provide hardware profiles but full remote attestation is limited by provider capabilities.
[07:36] Priya: Any concerns around model fine-tuning or data used for retraining?
[07:40] Samir: By default we do not use customer data to train shared models. We can provide isolated training pipelines if you want Redwood-managed fine-tuning under contract. That will be clearly scoped and use customer-managed keys for storage.
[07:55] Liam: Ok, good. One more commercial-ish question — what's the lead time for Private on-prem package?
[07:59] Samir: Typical on-prem packaging and validation is 8–12 weeks, Dedicated pools can be set up in 2–4 weeks depending on capacity and contract. Hosted is immediate with account provisioning.
[08:10] Priya: For audit logs retention we might need 7 years for some regulated products. Do you accommodate that?
[08:16] Emily: Yes, via customer-managed S3 buckets or long-term archive. There may be additional costs but we can support long-term retention and export for legal hold.
[08:26] Daniel: Can we get a sample data flow diagram that shows where keys live, where logs go, and what is retained?
[08:31] Emily: Yes, I'll include a diagram in the follow-up that maps Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private flows, KMS ownership, and log destinations.
[08:38] Samir: Let's talk about the next steps and POC scope. If you want we can run a lightweight POC on Hosted for a couple of non-sensitive routes to prove latency and cost, and a parallel Dedicated/Private architecture review.
[08:50] Liam: We'd prefer to start with an isolated Hosted POC and a Dedicated sizing conversation. If things look good, we'll pilot Private for PHI workloads.
[08:59] Priya: Agreed. Please include the security artifacts and contact info for your compliance team.
[09:04] Samir: Absolutely. I'll send SOC 2 summary and the compliance contacts. Emily will share the architecture note and POC checklist.
[09:12] Asha: For the POC we'll provide sample prompts and expected throughput.
[09:15] Samir: Perfect. Any final questions?
[09:18] Priya: One last thing — do you support per-request redaction hooks or client-side redaction? We want to ensure PII never leaves the client for certain routes.
[09:26] Emily: We have pre-call webhooks and redaction SDK patterns. You can also do client-side redaction before sending. We'll attach sample code.
[09:34] Liam: Great. Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the docs by end of week.
[09:40] [call ends]
